region.text: Colombo and its coast: the Portuguese sail to Colombo and treat with the King of Kotte; the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 1505: the Portuguese reach Ceylon and agree a trade treaty with the King of Kotte at Colombo. S1: "Portuguese presence in the island lasted from 1505 to 1658", infobox "Portuguese arrival: 1505". S2: they "arrived in Sri Lanka in 1505", landing at Galle Harbour, "sailed to Colombo" and "successfully secured a trade agreement with the King of Kotte during this first meeting". A presence and a treaty, not a conquest: no land is taken from Kotte, so no counterpart; the Colombo disc is my reading.

region.text: Mannar Island, wrested from the Jaffna kingdom

ledger.note: 1560: Viceroy Dom Constantino de Bragança's first expedition takes Mannar Island from Jaffna. S3: it "failed to subdue the kingdom but wrested Mannar Island from it". Matches the loss in the jaffna-kingdom dossier.

region.text: Colombo and the Kotte rump, under Portuguese protection

ledger.note: 1565: Dharmapala of Kotte takes refuge at Colombo under Portuguese protection. S2: Dharmapala abandoned the Kotte capital "due to repeated attacks from the Kingdom of Sitawaka" and "was taken to Colombo under Portuguese protection" (the paragraph is dated 1565); earlier the kingdom "became reliant on Portuguese assistance" (undated). The status as vassal is my reading of 'protection'; Kotte is its own state to 1597. 1580: Dharmapala "had bequeathed the Kingdom of Kotte to the Portuguese monarch" (S1), a claim, not rule.

region.text: the Jaffna kingdom paying tribute to the Portuguese

ledger.note: 1582: Jaffna is paying tribute to the Portuguese. S3: "by 1582 the Jaffna king was paying a tribute of ten elephants or an equivalent in cash" ("the circumstances are unclear"); 1591: after André Furtado de Mendonça's second expedition "king Puvirasa Pandaram was killed and his son Ethirimanna Cinkam was installed as the monarch". The page says 'by 1582'; the relation may be older.

region.text: the ports of Galle, Batticaloa and Trincomalee, Portuguese when the Dutch took them in 1639-1640

ledger.note: 1597 (bridging, page silent): Portuguese ports on the south and east coasts. None of the five pages opened says when or from whom the Portuguese took Galle, Batticaloa or Trincomalee; S4 shows them Portuguese when they fell ("Batticaloa and Trincomalee fell in 1639, Galle in 1640") and S1 dates Portuguese control of the island from 1597, which is the date used. A gap-filler should open 'Sinhalese–Portuguese War'.

27 May 1597: Dharmapala dies and Kotte passes to the Portuguese crown. S2 infobox "Disestablishment: 27 May 1597"; S1 "Death of Dharmapala of Kotte: 27 May 1597". The vassal relation ends in annexation (next event).

region.text: the Kotte Kingdom: Colombo, Gampaha and Kalutara districts without Sitawaka's core, as the Kotte dossier draws it

ledger.note: 1597: direct Portuguese rule begins in Ceylon with the cession of Kotte. S2: "In 1597, Dharmapala formally ceded the Kotte Kingdom to the Portuguese crown, marking the official end of the Kotte era"; S1: "controlled by the Portuguese Empire between 1597 and 1658", "direct Portuguese rule did not begin until after the death of Dharmapala" with a claim from the 1580 bequest. The page names the kingdom, not its districts: the region is the Kotte dossier's own shape (my reading). Jerónimo de Azevedo is listed as governor 1597-1614 (S1).

region.text: the city of Kandy, burned by the Portuguese

ledger.note: 1611: Portuguese forces capture Kandy. S4: "In 1611, Portuguese forces, acting in the name of the pretender Mayadunne of Uva, captured Kandy" "and once again set the city ablaze". Also S4: the Portuguese "briefly occupied Kandy in 1592" and invaded it in 1603.

1612 (bridging, page silent): the Portuguese leave Kandy. S4 gives no year for their leaving; the year mirrors the kingdom-of-kandy dossier's bridging end so that the pair closes; the kingdom continues under Senarat.
1619: the tributary kingdom of Jaffna is conquered. S3: Cankili II "confronted the Portuguese but was defeated, thus bringing the kingdom's independent existence to an end in 1619".

region.text: the Jaffna peninsula, to which the kingdom was "restricted" at its fall

ledger.note: 1619: the Portuguese conquer the Jaffna kingdom. S3: "By June 1619" there were two expeditions and the second, under Filipe de Oliveira, defeated Cankili II, who was "taken to Goa, where he was hanged"; the infobox names Portuguese Ceylon as the successor. S4: "In 1619, Cankili II was deposed and the Jaffna Kingdom absorbed into the Portuguese Empire." One S3 sentence dates the conquest to 1620.

1639: Batticaloa and Trincomalee fall. S4: "Batticaloa and Trincomalee fell in 1639"; S5: "The Dutch conquered Batticaloa in 1639". The Dutch as captor of Trincomalee is my reading (S4's sentence does not name the captor).
1640: the Dutch take Galle. S5: "The Dutch conquered Batticaloa in 1639 and Galle in 1640 before the alliance broke down"; S4: "Galle in 1640".

region.text: Colombo and the sea off it, where the Dutch and Portuguese fleets fought

ledger.note: 1654: the Dutch and Portuguese fight for Colombo. S5: "On 23 March 1654, a naval battle took place near Colombo" and "The 2 May 1654 action was a sea battle which took place near Colombo". The first dated action off Colombo; the land siege ("a six-month siege", S4) is undated on the pages opened.
1656: the contest for Colombo ends with the Dutch capture (next event).
1656: the Dutch capture Colombo. S5: "the Dutch captured Colombo in 1656"; S4: "the fall of Colombo after a six-month siege"; António de Amaral de Meneses is listed as governor 1656-1658 (S1).
June 1658: Jaffna falls. S1 infobox "Fall of Jaffna: June 1658".

region.text: what was left of the Portuguese holdings (the Kotte lowlands outside Colombo, Mannar) when the last Portuguese were driven out

ledger.note: 1658: the last Portuguese leave Ceylon. S5: the Dutch "drove the last Portuguese from Ceylon in 1658"; S1: "controlled ... between 1597 and 1658". The page does not say when the Kotte lowlands outside Colombo (Negombo, Kalutara) and Mannar fell between 1656 and 1658; they are closed with the state. 1661: Portugal "ceded the colonies of Ceylon (now Sri Lanka)" and paid eight million guilders (S5), a legal cession of land already lost.

wars.name: Sinhalese–Portuguese War
wars.outcome: The Portuguese held the coast and lost it to the Dutch (allies of Kandy from 1638); Kandy kept the interior.
wars.note: S4: "Kandy entered a long period of attritionary warfare with the Portuguese, starting with the Campaign of Danture" (1595); Kandy occupied by the Portuguese 1592 (brief), 1603 (invasion) and 1611; Randeniwela, 2 August 1630, "large parts of Portuguese Ceilao being overrun by the Kandyans"; Kandyan alliance with the Dutch from 1638 (S4: "In May of that year he concluded a wide-ranging alliance with the Dutch", 1638; S5 'from 1638 onward'); the alliance "remade in 1649" and broken by 1656 (S5, S4). S1 dates a Luso–Kandyan Treaty to 1633. The pages name no frontier lands, so zones is empty; the 1611 occupation of Kandy is in the ledger. The war's own page was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Jaffna kingdom
wars.outcome: Cankili II defeated by Filipe de Oliveira; the kingdom ended in 1619 and passed to Portuguese Ceylon.
wars.note: S3: Cankili II "confronted the Portuguese but was defeated" (1617-1619). Mannar Island was taken in 1560 and the king was a tributary by 1582.

wars.name: Dutch–Portuguese War
wars.outcome: The Dutch, first with Kandy, took Batticaloa (1639), Galle (1640), Colombo (1656) and Jaffna (June 1658); Portugal ceded Ceylon in 1661.
wars.note: Ceylon theatre only; S5 gives the whole war as 1598-1663. S5: "The Dutch intervened in the Sinhalese–Portuguese War on Ceylon from 1638 onward, initially as allies of the Kingdom of Kandy"; naval actions off Colombo 23 March and 2 May 1654; "After exploiting and then double-crossing their Kandyan allies, the Dutch captured Colombo in 1656 and drove the last Portuguese from Ceylon in 1658."

wars.name: Sitawaka attacks on Kotte
wars.outcome: Kotte lost most of its land to Sitawaka and its king took refuge at Colombo under Portuguese protection (1565); after Sitawaka fell in 1594 the lowlands were re-annexed to Kotte.
wars.note: S2: "due to repeated attacks from the Kingdom of Sitawaka, led by Mayadunne and his son Rajasinghe I" Dharmapala abandoned the capital; "after the downfall of Sitawaka in 1594, these areas were re-annexed to the Kotte kingdom". The land moves belong to the kingdom-of-kotte and kingdom-of-sitawaka dossiers; zones empty here.

certainty.note: A trading post and a protected Kotte, with no boundary on any page; the Colombo disc and the Mannar Island disc are the smallest regions the grid draws.

No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened (the Luso–Kandyan Treaty of 1633 has no terms on S1); the inland frontier against Kandy was fluid (S4) and the corrected shape is a minimum. Colombo, the Jaffna peninsula and Mannar Island are named places and the sharpest edges.

notes:
PORTUGUESE CEYLON (sa-06-a). Five pages opened (budget 5): Portuguese Ceylon (S1), Kingdom of Kotte (S2), Jaffna kingdom (S3), Kingdom of Kandy (S4), Dutch–Portuguese War (S5). WebFetch returned extracts, so quotes are as the extracts gave them; S1 itself is a stub (infobox and a few sentences, no territorial history, no area).

MAIN FINDING: ALL ELEVEN CLIOPATRIA SHAPES ARE WRONG. The 'Portuguese Ceylon' row (1507-1686) is not the Portuguese-held coast. Measured with the gazetteer (resolve of each shape against Natural Earth districts): every shape from 1507 to 1659 holds all 70 cells of the Kandy, Matale, Nuwara Eliya, Badulla, Moneragala, Kegalle and Polonnaruwa districts (the Kandyan upcountry; 64 of 70 in 1632-1658), plus the east (Batticaloa, Ampara), Hambantota and, from 1595, the whole north; it holds none of the 28 Sri Lankan cells of the Portuguese Colonies row's 1570 coast (West and South coast belt: Gampaha, Galle, Kalutara, Colombo, Matara, Puttalam). The two rows are complements. S4 puts the Kingdom of Kandy 'in the central and eastern portion of the island', S1 puts direct Portuguese rule at 1597-1658, so the row is at best a stand-in for the Sinhalese interior. After 1658 it is larger than ever (207 cells in 1659, 87% of the island) although S1 and S5 have the last Portuguese gone in 1658. The kingdom-of-kandy dossier says the overlap with this row 'has not been measured': it is 70/70 upcountry cells in 1507-1631. Its owner may use the row's upcountry cells to seed Kandy's shape (Kandy has no Cliopatria row); I did not edit that dossier.

CORRECTED SHAPE IS A MINIMUM. Only places the pages name are drawn: Colombo (25 km, 4 cells), Mannar Island (1 cell, taken 1560), the Kotte lowlands (9 cells, the kingdom-of-kotte dossier's own shape, from 27 May 1597), Galle, Batticaloa and Trincomalee (20 km each, 8 cells, Portuguese when they fell in 1639-1640), the Jaffna peninsula (region 'Jaffna', 8 cells, 1619). Total 20 cells (about 5,100 km2) from 1597, 28 cells (about 7,100 km2) from 1619. S4 says Randeniwela (2 August 1630) 'resulted in large parts of Portuguese Ceilao being overrun by the Kandyans' and that in 1639-1640 'Kandyan forces seized Portuguese territories further inland', so the Portuguese held more than this; no page opened names the lands. The Portuguese Colonies row draws a broader belt for 1640-1661 (122 Sri Lankan cells in 1645, Puttalam, Kurunegala, Anuradhapura, Ratnapura included) which am-06 accepted in portuguese-empire.json; I did not adopt it for want of a page. A gap-filler should open 'Sinhalese–Portuguese War' (and 'Siege of Colombo (1655-1656)', 'Battle of Randeniwela', 'Battle of Danture', 'Dutch Ceylon') to widen the shape and date the ports (the ledger's only confidence-1 gain, 1597, bridges that silence).

OVERLAPS TO RESOLVE IN THE COMPILE STEP. (1) portuguese-empire.json (am-06) reviews the Colonies row's Ceylon cells for 1564-1581 and 1640-1658 as Portuguese; this dossier draws Ceylon too. Recommended: portuguese-ceylon draws the island and the empire's Colonies shapes drop their Sri Lankan cells (28 in 1570, 122 in 1645). (2) During the Iberian Union (1582-1639) Cliopatria draws the Ceylon coast (Colombo, Gampaha, Galle, Kalutara, Puttalam, Mannar, Jaffna, Kurunegala, Anuradhapura) inside its Spanish Empire row; this dossier keeps the colony Portuguese (S1 lists Philip I, II and III as monarchs; spanish-empire has a vassal_start portuguese-empire in 1581). (3) Colombo 25 km is drawn by this dossier from 1505 and by kingdom-of-kotte for 1564-1593 (the Portuguese-protected rump); the vassal pair 1565-1597 tints it. (4) 'dutch-ceylon' is the counterpart of the 1639-1658 losses; the group's other part writes it and should carry the matching gains and start it by 1639 (Cliopatria's Dutch Ceylon row starts in 1687 and the Dutch Republic row holds the coast in 1659-1686). The inland losses to Kandy are not placed (pages name no lands).

DISAGREEMENTS AND LEFT OUT. S2's infobox gives the Kotte capital move as 1412 and the text 1415 (not mine). S3 dates the conquest of Jaffna to 1619 in most places and 1620 in one sentence: 1619 used. Sitawaka's fall is 1594 on S2 (the sitawaka dossier has 1593/1594). S4 gives the Danture campaign as 1595, the sitawaka dossier 1594. The Luso–Kandyan Treaty (1633, S1 infobox) has no terms on the pages, so it moves no border here. The 1661 cession (S5) is in the dissolve note, not an event, because the state ends in 1658. The brief Portuguese occupation of Kandy in 1592 and the invasion of 1603 (S4) are in the 1611 event and war notes, not paired events: the kingdom-of-kandy dossier has only the 1611-1612 pair, mirrored here (its 1612 end is bridging, conf 1).

IDENTITY. Start 1505 (S1 'Portuguese presence in the island lasted from 1505 to 1658'; Cliopatria starts 1507), end June 1658 (S1 'Fall of Jaffna: June 1658'). Type colony of the Portuguese Empire, family portugal. Rulers are the infobox monarchs (metropolitan); the governors the page lists are Jerónimo de Azevedo 1597-1614 and António de Amaral de Meneses 1656-1658, nothing between. Capital Colombo with no years on the page. Wikidata Q1709007; Cliopatria's umbrella (Portuguese Empire) lists the row as a member.

GAZETTEER NAMES USED. All resolve: Colombo, Galle, Batticaloa, Trincomalee, Kandy, Ratnapura (places); Kŏḷamba, Gampaha, Kaḷutara (admin1); region 'Jaffna'. Mannar Island has no place entry (only the district Mannārama), so it is a 15 km circle at 79.85E 9.0N; the gazetteer agent may add 'Mannar Island'.
